title: API: PATCH parts/status deactivates two parts, writes their history and lists them under status inactive
custom_preconds: Env https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com, S2 shop. Location Staging Heavy Duty. Logged in as (a) Admin or a default Parts Manager. API replay from Chrome DevTools against sv10647api.qa.shopview.com with header X-Location-ID = the current location (Copy as fetch from a request of the logged-in session, then edit method, path and body). QAPL-CAP-010 and QAPL-CAP-011 are active. After the test send the same PATCH with "status":"active" to restore them.
custom_steps:
1. GET /api/inventory/parts?status=active&search=QAPL-CAP-01 and note the ids of QAPL-CAP-010 and QAPL-CAP-011.
  2. PATCH /api/inventory/parts/status with body {"partIds":["<QAPL-CAP-010 id>","<QAPL-CAP-011 id>"],"status":"inactive","note":"Superseded by RC-500X"}.
  3. GET /api/inventory/parts?status=inactive&search=QAPL-CAP-01, then the same with status=active.
  4. GET /api/parts/history/<QAPL-CAP-010 id>, then the same for QAPL-CAP-011.
  5. Open /parts/history/<QAPL-CAP-010 id> and /parts/history/<QAPL-CAP-011 id> in the app.
custom_expected:
1. 200; both parts are in data.collection with is_active: true.
  2. 200 with data.updated listing both ids (with their part numbers) and data.failed: [].
  3. status=inactive lists both with is_active: false; status=active no longer lists them.
  4. Each part has one new status entry carrying the note "Superseded by RC-500X" (no DB access: this stands in for the DB check of entity_event part.status.deactivated with the note).
  5. Each reads "Deactivated | Reason: Superseded by RC-500X" with Staff = the logged-in user and the Date and Time of the call (no DB access: this stands in for the DB check of part.updated_by and updated_at).
